doc.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Miles, Donald Byrd, Newport Youth Band and first gigs
title: Declining gigs while measuring himself against Lee Morgan and Freddie Hubbard
summary: He refuses gigs because he doesn't feel ready next to trumpeters five years older, and they discuss jazz generations.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Did you sit in during that period?
I would go to places, but I was not taking any work. A lot of the guys would call me to work, Billy Mitchell, Ernie Wilkins, and I wouldn’t take any work. I was just practicing.
You didn’t think you were ready?

Uh, I didn’t think so because I was listening to Lee Morgan, and Booker Little, and Freddie Hubbard, all three that were great musicians and five years older than me. I couldn’t approach any of the stuff that they were doing, and that’s what I was practicing for, as well as Miles and Clifford Brown. You know, but those guys who were the closest to me, like Donald, he was different. He was 11 years older than me. But five years older than me, hey man, I figured I should be able to do that.
For five years, the jazz generations, we say are five years. That’s a big difference. It’s not like you have a friend that’s five years older. It’s interesting how those
generations…you know, Dizzy being five years older than…it completely changes things; doesn’t it?
